first_impression.reaction: Typed 'rhodes wedding venues' on the train. First line tells me the four parts of the island, the takeaways give me the one big-capacity venue and the paperwork, and there's a jump list. I'd read the takeaways, swipe through the table, tap Lindos, check the weather bit and the FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: Rhodes wedding venues sit in four parts of the island: Lindos and the south, Rhodes Town in the north, the east coast around Kallithea, and the west coast at Ixia.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first sentence, matches my search. Good start.

journey.quote: Choose an area first, because Lindos and the south suit a village or beach wedding, Rhodes Town suits a large reception near the medieval Old Town, and the coasts suit a resort week.
journey.reaction: Same four areas I just read. At least it says which one suits what, but it still feels like a repeat in the bit I always read.

journey.quote: A civil marriage of foreign nationals on Rhodes needs a certificate of no impediment valid for six months, officially translated into Greek and carrying an Apostille for non-EU countries.
journey.reaction: Says 'foreign nationals', not just Australians, so this works for me in Singapore too. Screenshot-worthy.

journey.section: Rhodes wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Setting | Ceremony options | Capacity |
journey.reaction: Five columns on a phone means swiping sideways, and when I get to Capacity it says 'Not published' for eight of the nine. Venue, area and ceremony are the useful bits.

journey.section: How to compare Rhodes venues like for like
journey.quote: Only one venue here publishes a reception figure: Grande Albergo delle Rose states seating for 450 guests.
journey.reaction: Third time I've seen the 450 (takeaways, table, now here) and it comes back again in the venue section. Same with Melenos and its three nights. Lots of scrolling to reread things.

journey.quote: Aquagrand publishes two named wedding packages, Aqua Pearl and Aqua Marine.
journey.reaction: This sits under the bold label 'Capacity, rooms and exclusive use', but it's about packages. Same at Atrium Palace, Atrium Platinum and Elysium, where that label is followed by restaurants and bridal suites. I scan bold labels, so this throws me.

journey.quote: Being adults-only matters if your guest list includes young children.
journey.reaction: Quick rule that rules it in or out. Useful.

journey.quote: The extras read like a weekend in the village: a rehearsal dinner on the Melenos terrace, a welcome cocktail party, a private boat excursion, and donkeys to carry the couple to the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Donkeys to the ceremony. Okay, that's the one I'd send to my sister.

journey.quote: Because of its popularity, it needs to be booked as far in advance as possible, so lock the chapel before anything else if it is the setting you want.
journey.reaction: Real, actionable tip. This is why I'd bookmark.

journey.quote: The prevailing wind at the Rodos station is westerly from January to November, so ask about sheltered spaces for an outdoor ceremony on this side.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that, and it's specific. Trust goes up.

journey.quote: For a summer date, plan shade, water for guests and a later ceremony, and follow local authorities' advice if a fire is reported.
journey.reaction: Heading says 'When to marry' and I get a table plus warnings, but nobody tells me which months to aim for. The numbers are right there; just say it.

journey.quote: The figures below come from the [Hellenic National Meteorological Service](http://oldportal.emy.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=South%20Aegean&poli=Rodos) Rodos station, data period 1955-2010.
journey.reaction: Is this still true in 2026? Data that stops in 2010 feels old, though the heatwave and wildfire bits below feel current.

journey.quote: Plan the Old Town as your portrait setting.
journey.reaction: I asked 'can we get married in the Old Town' and didn't get a yes or no. Are Rodini park and Monte Smith in the Old Town or not? I'm guessing it means no, but I had to work it out.

journey.quote: Can we have a wedding ceremony at St Paul's Bay?
journey.reaction: Exactly what I'd type, with a straight 'Yes' and names. Good FAQ.

journey.section: Getting legally married on Rhodes, in brief
journey.quote: The [Australian Embassy in Athens](https://greece.embassy.gov.au/athn/notarial.html) witnesses applications for and issues Certificates of No Impediment, and legalises original Australian public documents by authentication or apostille.
journey.reaction: Not for me as a Singaporean. The Greek-side rules above still help, so I just skip this bit.

journey.section: Shortlist your Rhodes venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: So it's an Australian service. Not sure they'd take me.

unanswered_questions: Which months are actually best for a Rhodes wedding? The page has the figures but never names a window.
Can we hold the ceremony inside the Old Town walls, yes or no?
Roughly what does a Rhodes venue cost? Even a ballpark would help.
Do you work with couples outside Australia?

turn_offs_found.quote: For a summer date, plan shade, water for guests and a later ceremony, and follow local authorities' advice if a fire is reported.
turn_offs_found.why: The 'When to marry in Rhodes' heading promises an answer and gives me a table and warnings instead. I wanted a month or two to aim for, and the page's own numbers already point to one.

turn_offs_found.quote: Aquagrand publishes two named wedding packages, Aqua Pearl and Aqua Marine.
turn_offs_found.why: Headings that don't match what's under them. The bold 'Capacity, rooms and exclusive use' label sits over packages, restaurants and bridal suites at several venues, so scanning the labels on my phone sends me to the wrong thing.

turn_offs_found.quote: Plan the Old Town as your portrait setting.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ question is yes/no and the answer dodges it. FAQs are where I expect the straight answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: Only one venue here publishes a reception figure: Grande Albergo delle Rose states seating for 450 guests.
turn_offs_found.why: The 450 and the Melenos three-night rule each appear three or four times (takeaways, table, compare section, venue section, FAQ). It's scrolling past the same facts.

would_share_with: My sister, for the Melenos donkeys and the St Paul's Chapel 'book it first' tip
A friend planning a Greek island wedding, for the takeaways and the foreign-nationals paperwork line

cta_reaction.quote: start your shortlist with Wedded Concierge
cta_reaction.why: I'm browsing, not planning yet. The links sit in the text with no pop-ups, so they didn't bother me. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and 'AUD for Australian couples' makes me think it isn't for me.

top_3_changes: Make 'When to marry in Rhodes' answer its heading: name the month window the page's own temperature, rain, heat and dust figures point to, in one line before the table.

Fix the venue labels so they match what follows: where 'Capacity, rooms and exclusive use' introduces packages, restaurants or bridal suites, rename the label or move those lines, and give the Old Town FAQ a direct yes or no in its first sentence.

Cut repetition for phone readers: swap the first takeaway (a repeat of the intro) for something new, and trim the repeated 450 and Melenos three-night lines in the compare section to a pointer; consider a narrower at-a-glance table so the useful columns fit without a sideways swipe.

Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
